claude.sample_unit: simulated patients in Markov model cohort
models_evaluated: gradient boosted trees HCV prediction algorithm (EMR-based)

links.outcome: Cost-effectiveness of predictive model at varying recall thresholds under $100k/QALY willingness-to-pay
links.effect: ML screening was cost-effective for recall up to 30%; optimal recall 30% (precision 0.27%), mean ICER $94,022/QALY; cost-saving below 5% recall.
links.quote: The ML algorithm was found to be cost-effective with recall levels up to 30% compared to status quo screening ( Figure 3 ).

unlisted_practices: Cost-effectiveness modeling (Markov model) of ML-enabled screening before deployment
Sensitivity analysis of lead-time and algorithm cost assumptions

models_evaluated: Gradient boosted trees ML algorithm for HCV prediction

links.effect: Optimal recall was 30% (Precision 0.27%), with mean ICER $94,022/QALY gained.
links.quote: The optimal recall level was 30% (Precision 0.27%), which resulted in a mean ICER of $94,022/QALY gained.

links.outcome: QALYs and costs versus conventional testing
links.effect: At 30% recall, costs increased $1.20/person and QALYs increased 0.000013/person versus conventional testing.
links.quote: At 30% recall, the algorithm required additional per-person costs of $1.20 [95% CI: $1.07, $1.31], yielding a 0.000013 [95% CI: 0.000010, 0.000016] increase in QALYs per person over conventional testing practices.
